newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coalition, SPD hint at thaw in tax, pension row.
newsitem.headline: Coalition, SPD hint at thaw in tax, pension row.

text.p: German coalition and opposition forces on Sunday showed the first signs that they could ease their deadlock over a 30-billion-mark tax cut proposal and a plan to reform the country's generous pension system.
The coalition was willing to whittle down the plan to reach a compromise with the Social Democrats (SPD), one of the architects of the tax plan told a German newspaper.

"We know very well that we have to be willing to negotiate and willing to compromise...even up to a certain degree against our political and economic judgement," Hans-Peter Repnik, tax negotiator for the ruling Christian Democrats (CDU), said in an interview with Der Tagesspiegel.
